data.title: Prompt
data.tagline: A prompt is the message you send the AI—the problem, requirements, and context all live in it, and it steers what the AI builds.
data.learningOutcome: You reach for the prompt first when results are off (add object, requirements, done-criteria), and you separate prompts from system prompts.
data.description: "Build a client quote list with client, amount, date, and status, stored locally, newest first"—that whole sentence is the prompt. The AI reads it before every move: specific wording lands specific results, while "make a nice tool" forces guessing. When results disappoint, refine the prompt before switching tools—add the object, the requirements, and what counts as done.

learning.assumes: You have chatted with an AI and asked it to build something.
learning.outcome: You reach for the prompt first when results are off (add object, requirements, done-criteria), and you separate prompts from system prompts.

distinctions.label: System Prompt
distinctions.explanation: System Prompt is the developer-preset role the user cannot see; Prompt is what you write in each turn.

distinctions.label: Context Engineering
distinctions.explanation: Prompt is one message you write; Context Engineering manages the whole set of sources, memory, and rules.

explanation.title: Say what you want—and what you don't
explanation.text: Exclusions like "no charts yet" or "no login" stop the AI from growing the tool on its own.

explanation.title: Give checkable done-criteria
explanation.text: "Works on mobile" and "add, edit, delete all work" give you and the AI the same ruler.

explanation.title: One round, one change
explanation.text: Changing many things at once hides which sentence caused the error. Change one, verify, then continue.

data.boundary: Your prompt is the message you send each time; the system prompt is the developer-preset "job description" you cannot see or edit—two layers of one request. Prompting is also not context engineering: the former is this one message, the latter manages sources, memory, and rules as a whole. Refining the prompt is the first lever—cheap and immediate; its ceiling is set by what the context holds.

lessonPractice.title: The AI's result is not what you wanted. What should you do first?

options.label: Make the request specific: object, fields, and what counts as done
options.feedback: Correct. The AI works from your prompt; off-target results usually mean missing information. Add "what, what not, and how to verify."

options.label: Switch to a different AI tool right away
options.feedback: A different tool still has to guess from the same vague request. Clarifying is almost always faster.

options.label: Keep saying "wrong, redo it" until it gets you
options.feedback: "Wrong" does not say what is wrong. Each redo burns time and quota; one specific sentence beats ten vague ones.

data.agentPrompt: Build a client quote list with client name, amount, date, and status, stored in the browser for now. Skip charts and export this round. Done means: add, edit, and delete all work, and it works on mobile too.
